arabic_blocks: [578] حدثنا عمران بن ميسرة حدثنا عبد الوارث حدثنا خالد الحذاء عن أبي قلابة عن أنس قال: ذكروا النار والناقوس فذكروا اليهود والنصارى فأمر بلال أن يشفع الأذان وأن يوتر الإقامة
english_blocks: ‘Imran ibn Maysarah related to us. ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. Khalid al-Hadhdha’ related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:
They mentioned fire and the bell, and mentioned the Jews and the Christians. Bilal was then ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly.

The historical chapter heading adds والإقامة; the selected digital and modern heading read only بدء الأذان. The first chapter introduction remains separately preserved, including the Quran excerpts; no English comparison verse numbering is imported.

arabic_blocks: [579] حدثنا محمود بن غيلان قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني نافع ان ابن عمر كان يقول كان المسلمون حين قدموا المدينة يجتمعون فيتحينون الصلاة ليس ينادى لها فتكلموا يوما في ذلك، فقال بعضهم اتخذوا ناقوسا مثل ناقوس النصارى، وقال بعضهم بل بوقا مثل قرن اليهود، فقال عمر أولا تبعثون رجلا ينادي بالصلاة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: يا بلال قم فناد بالصلاة
english_blocks: Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: Nafi‘ informed me that Ibn ‘Umar used to say:

When the Muslims arrived in Madinah, they would gather and estimate the time of prayer; no call was made for it. One day they discussed this. Some of them said: “Use a bell like the Christians’ bell.” Others said: “Rather, a trumpet like the Jews’ horn.” ‘Umar said: “Will you not send a man to call to prayer?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Bilal, stand up and call to prayer.”

notes: The complete ‘Abd al-Razzaq/Ibn Jurayj/Nafi‘ chain and direct question of ‘Umar remain. The English comparison’s explanatory first-to-suggest wording is not inserted. No unprinted bell or horn description is added.

arabic_blocks: [580] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن سماك بن عطية عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن أنس قال أمر بلال أن يشفع الأذان وأن يوتر الإقامة إلا الإقامة
english_blocks: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Simak ibn ‘Atiyyah, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:
Bilal was ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly, except the iqamah.

arabic_blocks: [581] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا عبد الوهاب قال: أخبرنا خالد الحذاء عن أبي قلابة عن أنس بن مالك قال لما كثر الناس قال: ذكروا ان يعلموا وقت الصلاة بشيء يعرفونه فذكروا ان يوروا نارا أو يضربوا ناقوسا فأمر بلال أن يشفع الأذان وأن يوتر الإقامة
english_blocks: Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab informed us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

When the people became numerous—he said—they discussed making the time of prayer known by something they would recognize. They mentioned lighting a fire or striking a bell. Bilal was then ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly.

notes: The digital source reads حدثنا محمد, then two أخبرنا formulas, and retains قال after لما كثر الناس. The modern print has حدثني محمد and identifies him as Ibn Salam; the historical print names Muhammad ibn Salam and ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi with different reporting formulas. These printed expansions and transmission variants are recorded, not silently substituted for the selected digital wording.

arabic_blocks: [582] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا إسماعيل بن إبراهيم حدثنا خالد عن أبي قلابة عن أنس قال أمر بلال أن يشفع الأذان وأن يوتر الإقامة قال إسماعيل فذكرت لأيوب، فقال إلا الإقامة
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. Khalid related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:
Bilal was ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly.
Isma‘il said: I mentioned this to Ayyub, and he said: “Except the iqamah.”

arabic_blocks: [583] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا نودي للصلاة أدبر الشيطان وله ضراط حتى لا يسمع التأذين فإذا قضي النداء أقبل حتى إذا ثوب بالصلاة أدبر حتى إذا قضي التثويب أقبل حتى يخطر بين المرء ونفسه يقول اذكر كذا اذكر كذا لما لم يكن يذكر حتى يظل الرجل لا يدري كم صلى
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away, passing wind, so that he does not hear the adhan. When the call is finished, he returns. Then, when the iqamah is called for prayer, he turns away. When the iqamah is finished, he returns, coming between a person and his own self, saying: ‘Remember such-and-such; remember such-and-such,’ about things he had not been remembering, until the man no longer knows how much he has prayed.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The repeated departures and returns, passing wind, two repeated reminders and uncertainty about the amount prayed remain. Tathwib is rendered as the iqamah in this context, consistent with both comparison accounts; no later devotional advice is inserted.

arabic_blocks: [584] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي صعصعة الأنصارى ثم المازني عن أبيه أنه أخبره أن أبا سعيد الخدري قال له إني أراك تحب الغنم والبادية فإذا كنت في غنمك أو باديتك فأذنت بالصلاة فارفع صوتك بالنداء فإنه لا يسمع مدى صوت المؤذن جن ولا إنس ولا شيء إلا شهد له يوم القيامة قال أبو سعيد سمعته من رسول الله ﷺ
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa‘sa‘ah al-Ansari, then al-Mazini, from his father, who informed him that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said to him:

“I see that you love sheep and the open country. When you are among your sheep or in your open country and give the call to prayer, raise your voice in the call. No jinn, human, or anything else that hears the reach of the caller’s voice will fail to bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection.”
Abu Sa‘id said: I heard this from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

arabic_blocks: [585] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن حميد عن أنس بن مالك أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا غزا بنا قوما لم يكن يغزو بنا حتى يصبح وينظر فإن سمع أذانا كف عنهم وإن لم يسمع أذانا أغار عليهم قال: فخرجنا إلى خيبر فانتهينا إليهم ليلا فلما أصبح ولم يسمع أذانا ركب وركبت خلف أبي طلحة وإن قدمي لتمس قدم النبي ﷺ قال: فخرجوا إلينا بمكاتلهم ومساحيهم فلما رأوا النبي ﷺ قالوا محمد والله محمد والخميس قال: فلما رآهم رسول الله ﷺ قال: الله أكبر الله أكبر خربت خيبر إنا إذا نزلنا بساحة قوم { فساء صباح المنذرين
english_blocks: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik:

That when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went on an expedition with us against a people, he would not attack them with us until morning, when he would observe. If he heard an adhan, he held back from them; if he did not hear an adhan, he raided them. He said: We went out to Khaybar and reached them at night. When morning came and he heard no adhan, he mounted, and I rode behind Abu Talhah; my foot was touching the Prophet’s foot, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: They came out towards us with their baskets and spades. When they saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they said: “Muhammad! By Allah, Muhammad and the army!” He said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw them, he said: “Allah is greatest! Allah is greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend upon a people’s courtyard, evil is the morning of those who have been warned.”

notes: Both Allahu akbar exclamations, each selected honorific, the foot contact, baskets and spades, and every narrative speech transition remain. The source has an unmatched opening brace before its closing Quran phrase; its Arabic characters remain untouched. The English translates that complete phrase and adds only sentence punctuation. The historical print reads يغير in the initial clause, whereas the selected digital and modern print have يغزو.

arabic_blocks: [586] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عطاء بن يزيد الليثي عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا سمعتم النداء فقولوا مثل ما يقول المؤذن

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you hear the call, say the same as the caller says.”

arabic_blocks: [587] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن محمد بن إبراهيم بن الحارث قال: حدثني عيسى بن طلحة أنه سمع معاوية يوما، فقال مثله إلى قوله وأشهد أن محمدا رسول الله
english_blocks: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, who said: ‘Isa ibn Talhah related to me:
That he heard Mu‘awiyah one day, and he said the same, up to his words: “And I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

arabic_blocks: [588] حدثنا إسحاق بن راهويه قال: حدثنا وهب بن جرير قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى نحوه قال يحيى وحدثني بعض إخواننا أنه قال لما قال حي على الصلاة قال لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله، وقال هكذا سمعنا نبيكم ﷺ يقول
english_blocks: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh related to us. He said: Wahb ibn Jarir related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya:
Something similar.
Yahya said: And some of our brothers related to me that he said:
When he said, “Come to prayer,” he said, “There is no power and no strength except through Allah.” And he said: “This is how we heard your Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, speak.”

The English comparison adds names and explanatory parentheticals absent from the selected Arabic; these are not inserted. Bewley’s unnumbered same-from-Yahya line is read with its 588 continuation.

arabic_blocks: [589] حدثنا علي بن عياش قال: حدثنا شعيب بن أبي حمزة عن محمد بن المنكدر عن جابر بن عبد الله أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: من قال حين يسمع النداء اللهم رب هذه الدعوة التامة والصلاة القائمة آت محمدا الوسيلة والفضيلة وابعثه مقاما محمودا الذي وعدته حلت له شفاعتي يوم القيامة
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Ayyash related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb ibn Abi Hamzah related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says, on hearing the call, ‘O Allah, Lord of this complete call and the prayer being established, grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and pre-eminence, and raise him to a praised station which You have promised him,’ my intercession will be due to him on the Day of Resurrection.”

notes: The Arabic technical noun الوسيلة remains al-Wasilah; it is not replaced with an expanded doctrinal definition. الفضيلة is rendered pre-eminence and مقاما محمودا a praised station. The translation does not add English comparison parentheses about Paradise or the Day of Judgment to the invocation. No additional invocation ending is supplied.

arabic_blocks: [590] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن سمي مولى أبي بكر عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال لو يعلم الناس ما في النداء والصف الأول ثم لم يجدوا إلا أن يستهموا عليه لاستهموا ولو يعلمون ما في التهجير لاستبقوا إليه ولو يعلمون ما في العتمة والصبح لأتوهما ولو حبوا
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If people knew what is in the call and the first row, and then found no way to obtain it except by drawing lots, they would draw lots. If they knew what is in going early, they would race to it. And if they knew what is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling.”

notes: The source has التهجير without naming Zuhr. Going early follows the general early-attendance sense reflected in Bewley, while the Khan-family comparison specifies Zuhr; that expansion is recorded but not inserted. The repeated conditions, first row, lots and crawling remain.

arabic_blocks: [591] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا حماد عن أيوب وعبد الحميد صاحب الزيادي وعاصم الأحول عن عبد الله بن الحارث قال خطبنا بن عباس في يوم ردغ فلما بلغ المؤذن حي على الصلاة فأمره أن ينادي الصلاة في الرحال فنظر القوم بعضهم إلى بعض، فقال: فعل هذا من هو خير منه وإنها عزمة

Ibn ‘Abbas addressed us on a muddy day. When the caller reached “Come to prayer,” he ordered him to call: “Prayer in your dwellings.” The people looked at one another. He said: “Someone better than him did this, and it is an obligation.”

arabic_blocks: [596] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا زهير قال: حدثنا سليمان التيمي عن أبي عثمان النهدي عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي ﷺ قال لا يمنعن أحدكم أو أحدا منكم أذان بلال من سحوره فإنه يؤذن أو ينادي بليل ليرجع قائمكم ولينبه نائمكم وليس أن يقول الفجر أو الصبح، وقال بأصابعه ورفعها إلى فوق وطأطأ إلى أسفل حتى يقول هكذا، وقال زهير بسبابتيه إحداهما فوق الأخرى ثم مدها عن يمينه وشماله
english_blocks: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Sulayman al-Taymi related to us, from Abu ‘Uthman al-Nahdi, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Let Bilal’s adhan not prevent any one of you—or anyone among you—from his pre-dawn meal, for he gives the adhan—or calls—at night, so that those of you standing in prayer may return and those of you sleeping may awaken. Dawn—or morning—is not like this”—and he gestured with his fingers, raising them upwards and lowering them downwards—“until it is like this.”
And Zuhayr gestured with his two index fingers, one above the other, then extended them to his right and left.

When the caller gave the adhan, some Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would stand and hurry towards the pillars, until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out while they were like that, praying the two rak‘ahs before Maghrib. There was no interval between the adhan and the iqamah.
‘Uthman ibn Jabalah and Abu Dawud said, from Shu‘bah: There was only a little between them.

The caller wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler.” Then he wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler.” Then he wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler,” until the shadow equalled the hillocks. arabic_blocks: [621] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيب وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أن أبا هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: تفضل صلاة الجميع صلاة أحدكم وحده بخمسة وعشرين جزءا وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار في صلاة الفجر ثم يقول أبو هريرة فاقرؤوا إن شئتم { إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا } قال شعيب وحدثني نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر قال تفضلها بسبع وعشرين درجة
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:
“Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of one of you alone by twenty-five parts. The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Fajr prayer.”
Then Abu Hurayrah says: “Recite, if you wish: ‘Indeed, the recitation at dawn is witnessed.’”
Shu‘ayb said: And Nafi‘ related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: “It surpasses it by twenty-seven degrees.”

arabic_blocks: [624] حدثنا قتيبة عن مالك عن سمي مولى أبي بكر عن أبي صالح السمان عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: بينما رجل يمشي بطريق وجد غصن شوك على الطريق فأخره فشكر الله له فغفر له، ثم قال الشهداء خمسة المطعون والمبطون والغريق وصاحب الهدم والشهيد في سبيل الله، وقال لو يعلم الناس ما في النداء والصف الأول ثم لم يجدوا إلا أن يستهموا لاستهموا عليه ولو يعلمون ما في التهجير لاستبقوا إليه ولو يعلمون ما في العتمة والصبح لأتوهما ولو حبوا
english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and moved it aside. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him.” Then he said: “The martyrs are five: one who dies of plague, one who dies of an abdominal illness, one who drowns, one who dies under a collapsed structure, and one martyred in the path of Allah.” And he said: “If people knew what there is in the call and the first row, then found no way except to draw lots, they would draw lots for it. If they knew what there is in going early, they would race to it. If they knew what there is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling.”

arabic_blocks: [625] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب قال: حدثنا عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا حميد عن أنس قال: قال النبي ﷺ يا بني سلمة ألا تحتسبون آثاركم، وقال مجاهد في قوله { ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم } قال خطاهم، وقال ابن أبي مريم أخبرنا يحيى بن أيوب حدثني حميد حدثني أنس أن بني سلمة أرادوا أن يتحولوا عن منازلهم فينزلوا قريبا من النبي ﷺ قال: فكره رسول الله ﷺ أن يعروا المدينة، فقال ألا تحتسبون آثاركم قال مجاهد خطاهم آثارهم أن يمشي في الأرض بأرجلهم
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Humayd related to us, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“Banu Salimah, will you not seek reward for your footsteps?”
And Mujahid said concerning His words, “And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces”: He said: “Their footsteps.”
And Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me. Anas related to me:

That Banu Salimah wanted to move from their homes and settle near the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disliked their leaving Madinah deserted, and said: “Will you not seek reward for your footsteps?”
Mujahid said: “Their footsteps are their traces: walking on the earth with their feet.”

“No prayer is heavier upon the hypocrites than Fajr and ‘Isha’. If they knew what there is in them, they would come to them even crawling. I considered ordering the caller to give the iqamah, then ordering a man to lead the people, then taking flames of fire and setting fire to those who have not yet gone out to prayer.”

arabic_blocks: [629] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني خبيب بن عبد الرحمن عن حفص بن عاصم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال: سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله الإمام العادل وشاب نشأ في عبادة ربه ورجل قلبه معلق في المساجد ورجلان تحابا في الله اجتمعا عليه وتفرقا عليه ورجل طلبته امرأة ذات منصب وجمال، فقال إني أخاف الله ورجل تصدق أخفى حتى لا تعلم شماله ما تنفق يمينه ورجل ذكر الله خاليا ففاضت عيناه
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Seven will Allah shade in His shade on a day when there is no shade except His shade: a just imam; a young person who grew up worshipping his Lord; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who loved one another for Allah’s sake, meeting on that basis and parting on that basis; a man whom a woman of rank and beauty sought, who said, ‘I fear Allah’; a man who gave charity and concealed it so that his left hand did not know what his right hand spent; and a man who remembered Allah alone, and his eyes overflowed.”

english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, who said:
And Anas was asked: “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, have a ring?”

He said: “Yes. One night he delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer until halfway through the night. Then, after he had prayed, he turned his face towards us and said: ‘The people have prayed and slept, and you have continued to be in prayer since you began waiting for it.’” He said: “It is as though I am looking at the gleam of his ring.”

english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mutarrif informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:
“Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning and in the evening, Allah prepares hospitality for him in Paradise each time he goes in the morning or the evening.”

arabic_blocks: [632] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن أبيه عن حفص بن عاصم عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة قال مر النبي ﷺ برجل قال وحدثني عبد الرحمن قال: حدثنا بهز بن أسد قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني سعد بن إبراهيم قال: سمعت حفص بن عاصم قال: سمعت رجلا من الأزد يقال له مالك بن بحينة أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى رجلا وقد أقيمت الصلاة يصلي ركعتين فلما انصرف رسول الله ﷺ لاث به الناس، وقال له رسول الله ﷺ الصبح أربعا الصبح أربعا تابعه غندر ومعاذ عن شعبة في مالك، وقال ابن إسحاق عن سعد عن حفص عن عبد الله بن بحينة، وقال حماد أخبرنا سعد عن حفص عن مالك
english_blocks: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from his father, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah, who said:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man.

He said: And ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me. He said: Bahz ibn Asad related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed me. He said: I heard Hafs ibn ‘Asim say: I heard a man from al-Azd called Malik ibn Buhaynah say:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man praying two rak‘ahs when the iqamah had been given. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, the people gathered around him, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “The dawn prayer as four? The dawn prayer as four?”
Ghundar and Mu‘adh corroborated it from Shu‘bah concerning Malik. And Ibn Ishaq said: From Sa‘d, from Hafs, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Buhaynah. And Hammad said: Sa‘d informed us, from Hafs, from Malik.

arabic_blocks: [633] حدثنا عمر بن حفص بن غياث قال: حدثني أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن إبراهيم قال الأسود قال كنا عند عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فذكرنا المواظبة على الصلاة والتعظيم لها قالت لما مرض رسول الله ﷺ مرضه الذي مات فيه فحضرت الصلاة فأذن، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فقيل له إن أبا بكر رجل أسيف إذا قام في مقامك لم يستطع أن يصلي بالناس وأعاد فأعادوا له فأعاد الثالثة، فقال إنكن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فخرج أبو بكر فصلى فوجد النبي ﷺ من نفسه خفة فخرج يهادي بين رجلين كأني أنظر إلى رجليه تخطان من الوجع فأراد أبو بكر أن يتأخر فأومأ إليه النبي ﷺ أن مكانك ثم أتي به حتى جلس إلى جنبه قيل للأعمش وكان النبي ﷺ يصلي وأبو بكر يصلي بصلاته والناس يصلون بصلاة أبي بكر، فقال برأسه نعم رواه أبو داود عن شعبة عن الأعمش بعضه وزاد أبو معاوية جلس عن يسار أبي بكر فكان أبو بكر يصلي قائما
english_blocks: ‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Ibrahim, who said: Al-Aswad said:

We were with ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and we mentioned constancy in prayer and the great regard due to it. She said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, the time for prayer came and the adhan was given. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” He was told: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He repeated it, and they repeated it to him. He repeated it a third time and said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr went out and prayed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out supported between two men. It is as though I can see his feet dragging from the pain. Abu Bakr wanted to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Then he was brought until he sat beside him.

Al-A‘mash was asked: “Was the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying, with Abu Bakr praying following his prayer, and the people praying following Abu Bakr’s prayer?” He nodded yes.
Abu Dawud related part of it from Shu‘bah, from al-A‘mash. Abu Mu‘awiyah added: “He sat to Abu Bakr’s left, and Abu Bakr prayed standing.”

arabic_blocks: [634] حدثنا إبراهيم بن موسى قال: أخبرنا هشام بن يوسف عن معمر عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله قال: قالت عائشة لما ثقل النبي ﷺ واشتد وجعه استأذن أزواجه أن يمرض في بيتي فأذن له فخرج بين رجلين تخط رجلاه الأرض وكان بين العباس ورجل آخر قال عبيد الله فذكرت ذلك لابن عباس ما قالت عائشة، فقال لي وهل تدري من الرجل الذي لم تسم عائشة قلت لا قال هو علي بن أبي طالب
english_blocks: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me. He said: ‘A’ishah said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and his pain intensified, he asked his wives’ permission to be cared for in my house, and they gave him permission. He went out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. He was between al-‘Abbas and another man.
‘Ubayd Allah said: I mentioned to Ibn ‘Abbas what ‘A’ishah had said. He said to me: “Do you know who the man was whom ‘A’ishah did not name?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib.”

arabic_blocks: [635] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع ان ابن عمر إذن بالصلاة في ليلة ذات برد وريح، ثم قال ألا صلوا في الرحال، ثم قال إن رسول الله ﷺ كان يأمر المؤذن إذا كانت ليلة ذات برد ومطر يقول ألا صلوا في الرحال

That Ibn ‘Umar gave the adhan for prayer on a cold, windy night. Then he said: “Listen, pray in your dwellings.” Then he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to instruct the caller, when it was a cold, rainy night, to say: ‘Listen, pray in your dwellings.’”

arabic_blocks: [636] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن ابن شهاب عن محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى أن عتبان بن مالك كان يؤم قومه وهو أعمى وأنه قال لرسول الله ﷺ يا رسول الله إنها تكون الظلمة والسيل وأنا رجل ضرير البصر فصل يا رسول الله في بيتي مكانا أتخذه مصلى فجاءه رسول الله ﷺ، فقال أين تحب أن أصلي فأشار إلى مكان من البيت فصلى فيه رسول الله ﷺ
english_blocks: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari:

He said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Messenger of Allah, there is darkness and floodwater, and I am a man with impaired sight. Pray, Messenger of Allah, in a place in my house that I can take as a place of prayer.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: “Where would you like me to pray?” He pointed to a place in the house, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed there.

arabic_blocks: [637] حدثنا عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد قال: حدثنا عبد الحميد صاحب الزيادي قال: سمعت عبد الله بن الحارث قال خطبنا بن عباس في يوم ذي ردغ فأمر المؤذن لما بلغ حي على الصلاة قال قل الصلاة في الرحال فنظر بعضهم إلى بعض فكأنهم أنكروا، فقال: كانكم أنكرتم هذا إن هذا فعله من هو خير مني يعني النبي ﷺ إنها عزمة وإني كرهت أن أحرجكم وعن حماد عن عاصم عن عبد الله بن الحارث عن ابن عباس نحوه غير أنه قال كرهت أن أؤثمكم فتجيئون تدوسون الطين إلى ركبكم
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith say:

Ibn ‘Abbas addressed us on a muddy day. When the caller reached “Come to prayer,” he instructed him, saying: “Say: ‘Prayer in the dwellings.’” Some of them looked at one another, as though they disapproved. He said: “It seems that you disapprove of this. Someone better than me did this”—meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. “It is a binding duty, and I disliked putting you in hardship.”

And from Hammad, from ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn ‘Abbas, something similar, except that he said: “I disliked causing you to incur sin, so that you would come trudging through mud up to your knees.”

arabic_blocks: [638] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة قال: سألت أبا سعيد الخدري، فقال جاءت سحابة فمطرت حتى سال السقف وكان من جريد النخل فأقيمت الصلاة فرأيت رسول الله ﷺ يسجد في الماء والطين حتى رأيت أثر الطين في جبهته

I asked Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, and he said:

A cloud came and rained until the roof leaked. It was made of palm fronds. The iqamah was given, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in the water and mud, until I saw the mark of mud on his forehead.

arabic_blocks: [639] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا أنس بن سيرين قال: سمعت أنسا يقول: قال رجل من الأنصار إني لا أستطيع الصلاة معك وكان رجلا ضخما فصنع للنبي ﷺ طعاما فدعاه إلى منزله فبسط له حصيرا ونضح طرف الحصير صلى عليه ركعتين، فقال رجل من آل الجارود لأنس أكان النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى قال: ما رأيته صلاها إلا يومئذ
english_blocks: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said: I heard Anas say:

A man of the Ansar said: “I am unable to pray with you.” He was a large man. He prepared food for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and invited him to his house. He spread a mat for him and sprinkled water on the edge of the mat. He prayed two rak‘ahs on it.
A man from the family of al-Jarud said to Anas: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha?” He said: “I never saw him pray it except on that day.”

arabic_blocks: [642] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل عن أبي أسامة عن عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: إذا وضع عشاء أحدكم وأقيمت الصلاة فابدؤوا بالعشاء ولا يعجل حتى يفرغ منه وكان ابن عمر يوضع له الطعام وتقام الصلاة فلا يأتيها حتى يفرغ وإنه ليسمع قراءة الإمام، وقال زهير ووهب بن عثمان عن موسى بن عقبة عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال النبي ﷺ إذا كان أحدكم على الطعام فلا يعجل حتى يقضي حاجته منه وإن أقيمت الصلاة رواه إبراهيم بن المنذر عن وهب بن عثمان ووهب مديني
english_blocks: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“When supper is set out for one of you and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper, and he should not hurry until he has finished it.”
Food would be set out for Ibn ‘Umar and the iqamah would be given, but he would not go to it until he had finished, while he could hear the imam reciting.
And Zuhayr and Wahb ibn ‘Uthman said: From Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“When one of you is eating, he should not hurry until he has satisfied his need for it, even if the iqamah has been given.”
Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related it from Wahb ibn ‘Uthman, and Wahb is from Madinah.

english_blocks: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

Malik ibn al-Huwayrith came to us in this mosque of ours and said: “I am indeed leading you in prayer, but prayer is not my purpose. I pray as I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray.”

I said to Abu Qilabah: “How did he pray?” He said: “Like this elder of ours.” He said: He was an elderly man who would sit when he raised his head from prostration, before standing up in the first rak‘ah.

arabic_blocks: [646] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا حسين عن زائدة عن عبد الملك بن عمير قال: حدثني أبو بردة عن أبي موسى قال مرض النبي ﷺ فاشتد مرضه، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس قالت عائشة إنه رجل رقيق إذا قام مقامك لم يستطيع أن يصلي بالناس قال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فعادت، فقال مري أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فإنكن صواحب يوسف فأتاه الرسول فصلى بالناس في حياة النبي ﷺ
english_blocks: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from Za’idah, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, who said: Abu Burdah related to me, from Abu Musa, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill, and his illness grew severe. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “He is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” She repeated it, and he said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. You are the women associated with Yusuf.” The messenger came to him, and he led the people in prayer during the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

arabic_blocks: [647] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها أنها قالت أن رسول الله ﷺ قال في مرضه مروا أبا بكر يصلي بالناس قالت عائشة قلت: إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس فقالت عائشة فقلت لحفصة قولي له إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس ففعلت حفصة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: مه إنكن لأنتن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل للناس فقالت حفصة لعائشة ما كنت لأصيب منك خيرا
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that she said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said: “If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said to Hafsah: “Say to him: ‘If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.’” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Stop! You are indeed the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to ‘A’ishah: “I was never to get any good from you.”

arabic_blocks: [648] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أنس بن مالك الأنصارى وكان تبع النبي ﷺ وخدمه وصحبه أن أبا بكر كان يصلي لهم في وجع النبي ﷺ الذي توفي فيه حتى إذا كان يوم الإثنين وهم صفوف في الصلاة فكشف النبي ﷺ ستر الحجرة ينظر إلينا وهو قائم كأن وجهه ورقة مصحف ثم تبسم يضحك فهممنا أن نفتتن من الفرح برؤية النبي ﷺ فنكص أبو بكر على عقبيه ليصل الصف وظن أن النبي ﷺ خارج إلى الصلاة فأشار إلينا النبي ﷺ أن أتموا صلاتكم وأرخى الستر فتوفي من يومه
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari informed me—he had followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, served him and kept his company:

That Abu Bakr used to lead them in prayer during the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in which he died. Then, on Monday, while they were in rows in prayer, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew back the curtain of the room and looked towards us while standing. His face was like a page of a copy of the Qur’an. Then he smiled, laughing. We almost became distracted by the joy of seeing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr stepped backwards to join the row, thinking that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was coming out to prayer. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to us to complete our prayer and let the curtain fall. He died that day.

arabic_blocks: [649] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز عن أنس قال لم يخرج النبي ﷺ ثلاثا فأقيمت الصلاة فذهب أبو بكر يتقدم، فقال نبي الله ﷺ بالحجاب فرفعه فلما وضح وجه النبي ﷺ ما نظرنا منظرا كان أعجب إلينا من وجه النبي ﷺ حين وضح لنا فأومأ النبي ﷺ بيده إلى أبي بكر أن يتقدم وأرخى النبي ﷺ الحجاب فلم يقدر عليه حتى مات
english_blocks: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not come out for three days. The iqamah was given, and Abu Bakr went forward. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the curtain and lifted it. When the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, appeared, we had never seen a sight more pleasing to us than the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it appeared to us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured with his hand to Abu Bakr to go forward. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, let the curtain fall, and he could not be reached until he died.

arabic_blocks: [650] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثنا ابن وهب قال: حدثني يونس عن ابن شهاب عن حمزة بن عبد الله أنه أخبره عن أبيه قال لما اشتد برسول الله ﷺ وجعه قيل له في الصلاة، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس قالت عائشة إن أبا بكر رجل رقيق إذا قرأ غلبه البكاء، فقال مروه فيصلي فعاودته قال مروه فيصلي إنكن صواحب يوسف تابعه الزبيدي وابن أخي الزهري وإسحاق بن يحيى الكلبي عن الزهري، وقال عقيل ومعمر عن الزهري عن حمزة عن النبي ﷺ
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah ibn ‘Abd Allah, that he informed him from his father, who said:

When the pain of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, grew severe, prayer was mentioned to him. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. When he recites, weeping overcomes him.” He said: “Tell him, and let him pray.” She repeated it to him. He said: “Tell him, and let him pray. You are the women associated with Yusuf.”

Al-Zubaydi, the nephew of al-Zuhri, and Ishaq ibn Yahya al-Kalbi corroborated it from al-Zuhri. And ‘Uqayl and Ma‘mar said: From al-Zuhri, from Hamzah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

arabic_blocks: [651] حدثنا زكريا بن يحيى قال: حدثنا ابن نمير قال: أخبرنا هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت أمر رسول الله ﷺ أبا بكر أن يصلي بالناس في مرضه فكان يصلي بهم قال عروة فوجد رسول الله ﷺ في نفسه خفة فخرج فإذا أبو بكر يؤم الناس فلما رآه أبو بكر استأخر فأشار إليه أن كما أنت فجلس رسول الله ﷺ حذاء أبي بكر إلى جنبه فكان أبو بكر يصلي بصلاة رسول الله ﷺ والناس يصلون بصلاة أبي بكر
english_blocks: Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer during his illness, and he used to lead them.

‘Urwah said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out while Abu Bakr was leading the people. When Abu Bakr saw him, he moved back, but he gestured to him to stay as he was. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat beside Abu Bakr, at his side. Abu Bakr prayed following the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people prayed following Abu Bakr’s prayer.

arabic_blocks: [652] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي حازم بن دينار عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي أن رسول الله ﷺ ذهب إلى بني عمرو بن عوف ليصلح بينهم فحانت الصلاة فجاء المؤذن إلى أبي بكر، فقال أتصلي للناس فأقيم قال: نعم فصلى أبو بكر فجاء رسول الله ﷺ والناس في الصلاة فتخلص حتى وقف في الصف فصفق الناس وكان أبو بكر لا يلتفت في صلاته فلما أكثر الناس التصفيق التفت فرأى رسول الله ﷺ فأشار إليه رسول الله ﷺ أن امكث مكانك فرفع أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه يديه فحمد الله على ما أمره به رسول الله ﷺ من ذلك ثم استأخر أبو بكر حتى استوى في الصف وتقدم رسول الله ﷺ فصلى فلما انصرف قال: يا أبا بكر ما منعك أن تثبت إذ أمرتك، فقال أبو بكر ما كان لابن أبي قحافة أن يصلي بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ما لي رأيتكم أكثرتم التصفيق من رابه شيء في صلاته فليسبح فإنه إذا سبح التفت إليه وإنما التصفيق للنساء
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu Hazim ibn Dinar, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf to reconcile them. The time for prayer came, and the caller came to Abu Bakr and said: “Will you lead the people in prayer, so that I may give the iqamah?” He said: “Yes.” Abu Bakr prayed. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came while the people were praying and made his way through until he stood in the row. The people clapped. Abu Bakr did not turn around during his prayer, but when the people clapped repeatedly, he turned and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, raised his hands and praised Allah for what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had instructed him to do. Then Abu Bakr moved back until he stood in the row, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went forward and prayed. When he had finished, he said: “Abu Bakr, what prevented you from remaining when I instructed you?” Abu Bakr said: “It was not for Ibn Abi Quhafah to pray in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Why did I see you clapping so much? Whoever is troubled by something in his prayer should glorify Allah, for when he glorifies Allah, attention is turned towards him. Clapping is for women.”

arabic_blocks: [653] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن مالك بن الحويرث قال قدمنا على النبي ﷺ ونحن شببة فلبثنا عنده نحوا من عشرين ليلة وكان النبي ﷺ رحيما، فقال لو رجعتم إلى بلادكم فعلمتموهم مروهم فليصلوا صلاة كذا في حين كذا وصلاة كذا في حين كذا وإذا حضرت الصلاة فليؤذن لكم أحدكم وليؤمكم أكبركم
english_blocks: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, who said:

We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as young men and stayed with him for about twenty nights. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was merciful. He said: “Why not return to your lands and teach them? Instruct them to pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time, and such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

arabic_blocks: [654] حدثنا معاذ بن أسد أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع قال: سمعت عتبان بن مالك الأنصارى قال استأذن النبي ﷺ فأذنت له، فقال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك فأشرت له إلى المكان الذي أحب فقام وصففنا خلفه ثم سلم وسلمنا
english_blocks: Mu‘adh ibn Asad related to us. ‘Abd Allah informed us. Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He said: I heard ‘Itban ibn Malik al-Ansari say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission, and I gave him permission. He said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” I pointed out the place I liked. He stood, and we formed rows behind him. Then he gave the salutation of peace, and we gave the salutation of peace.

arabic_blocks: [655] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا زائدة عن موسى بن أبي عائشة عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة قال دخلت على عائشة فقلت: ألا تحدثيني عن مرض رسول الله ﷺ قالت بلى ثقل النبي ﷺ، فقال أصلى الناس قلنا لا هم ينتظرونك قال ضعوا لي ماء في المخضب قالت ففعلنا فاغتسل فذهب لينوء فأغمي عليه ثم أفاق، فقال ﷺ أصلى الناس قلنا لا هم ينتظرونك يا رسول الله قال ضعوا لي ماء في المخضب قالت فقعد فاغتسل ثم ذهب لينوء فأغمي عليه ثم أفاق، فقال أصلى الناس قلنا لا هم ينتظرونك يا رسول الله، فقال ضعوا لي ماء في المخضب فقعد فاغتسل ثم ذهب لينوء فأغمي عليه ثم أفاق، فقال أصلى الناس فقلنا لا هم ينتظرونك يا رسول الله والناس عكوف في المسجد ينتظرون النبي عليه السلام لصلاة العشاء الآخرة فأرسل النبي ﷺ إلى أبي بكر بأن يصلي بالناس فأتاه الرسول، فقال إن رسول الله ﷺ يأمرك أن تصلي بالناس، فقال أبو بكر وكان رجلا رقيقا يا عمر صل بالناس، فقال له عمر أنت أحق بذلك فصلى أبو بكر تلك الأيام ثم إن النبي ﷺ وجد من نفسه خفة فخرج بين رجلين أحدهما العباس لصلاة الظهر وأبو بكر يصلي بالناس فلما رآه أبو بكر ذهب ليتأخر فأومأ إليه النبي ﷺ بأن لا يتأخر قال أجلساني إلى جنبه فأجلساه إلى جنب أبي بكر قال: فجعل أبو بكر يصلي وهو يأتم بصلاة النبي ﷺ والناس بصلاة أبي بكر والنبي ﷺ قاعد قال عبيد الله فدخلت على عبد الله بن عباس فقلت له ألا أعرض عليك ما حدثتني عائشة عن مرض النبي ﷺ قال: هات فعرضت عليه حديثها فما أنكر شيئا غير أنه قال أسمت لك الرجل الذي كان مع العباس قلت لا قال هو علي
english_blocks: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Musa ibn Abi ‘A’ishah, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, who said:

I visited ‘A’ishah and said: “Will you tell me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” She said: “Yes. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’” She said: “We did so, and he bathed. He tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’” She said: “He sat and bathed, then tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’ He sat and bathed, then tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ The people remained in the mosque, waiting for the Prophet, peace be upon him, for the later ‘Isha’ prayer.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. The messenger came to him and said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructs you to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr, who was a tender-hearted man, said: “‘Umar, lead the people in prayer.” ‘Umar said to him: “You have more right to do so.” Abu Bakr led the prayers during those days. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out between two men, one of them al-‘Abbas, for the Zuhr prayer. Abu Bakr was leading the people. When Abu Bakr saw him, he began to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him not to move back. He said: “Seat me beside him.” They seated him beside Abu Bakr. He said: Abu Bakr then prayed following the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people followed Abu Bakr’s prayer, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was seated.

‘Ubayd Allah said: I visited ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas and said to him: “Shall I present to you what ‘A’ishah related to me about the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: “Go ahead.” I presented her account to him, and he disputed nothing, except that he said: “Did she name for you the man who was with al-‘Abbas?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali.”

A man approached with two water-carrying camels when night had fallen. He found Mu‘adh praying, so he left his camel and went towards Mu‘adh. He recited Surat al-Baqarah or al-Nisa’. The man left, and word reached him that Mu‘adh had spoken against him. He went to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and complained to him about Mu‘adh. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Mu‘adh, are you one who repeatedly causes trial—or one who causes trial?”—three times. “Why did you not pray with ‘Glorify the name of your Lord,’ ‘By the sun and its brightness,’ and ‘By the night when it covers’? For behind you pray the elderly, the weak and those with a need.”
I think this is in the hadith.

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Sa‘id ibn Masruq, Mis‘ar and al-Shaybani followed him in narrating it. ‘Amr, ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam and Abu al-Zubayr said, from Jabir: Mu‘adh recited al-Baqarah in ‘Isha’. Al-A‘mash followed him in narrating it from Muharib.

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, someone came to inform him of the prayer. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” I said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will weep and be unable to recite.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” I said the same. On the third or fourth occasion, he said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” He led the prayer, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out supported between two men. It is as if I can see him tracing the ground with his feet. When Abu Bakr saw him, he began to move back. He gestured to him to pray. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, moved back, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat beside him, while Abu Bakr made the people hear the takbir.

english_blocks: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill, Bilal came to inform him of the prayer. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” I said: “Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. Whenever he stands in your place, he will not make the people hear. If only you would instruct ‘Umar.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” I said to Hafsah: “Tell him: ‘Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. Whenever he stands in your place, he will not make the people hear. If only you would instruct ‘Umar.’” He said: “Indeed, you are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

When he began the prayer, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief. arabic_blocks: [698] حدثنا عبد الأعلى بن حماد قال: حدثنا وهيب قال: حدثنا موسى بن عقبة عن سالم أبي النضر عن بسر بن سعيد عن زيد بن ثابت أن رسول الله ﷺ اتخذ حجرة قال حسبت أنه قال من حصير في رمضان فصلى فيها ليالي فصلى بصلاته ناس من أصحابه فلما علم بهم جعل يقعد فخرج إليهم، فقال قد عرفت الذي رأيت من صنيعكم فصلوا أيها الناس في بيوتكم فإن أفضل الصلاة صلاة المرء في بيته إلا المكتوبة قال عفان حدثنا وهيب حدثنا موسى سمعت أبا النضر عن بسر عن زيد عن النبي ﷺ
english_blocks: ‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us, from Salim Abu al-Nadr, from Busr ibn Sa‘id, from Zayd ibn Thabit:
That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made a small room—
He said: “I think he said: of a mat”—

in Ramadan. He prayed in it for several nights, and some of his Companions followed his prayer. When he became aware of them, he began to remain seated. He went out to them and said: “I have understood what I saw you doing. People, pray in your houses, for the best prayer is a person’s prayer in his house, except the prescribed prayer.”
‘Affan said: Wuhayb related to us. Musa related to us: I heard Abu al-Nadr, from Busr, from Zayd, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
